after.worked_solution:
Let's set $u=\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x).$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{2x}\cdot 2=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $e/2$ | ${e}^{2}/2$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $1$ | $2$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{e/2}^{{e}^{2}/2}\frac{2}{3x\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\,\text{d}x & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{e/2}^{{e}^{2}/2}\frac{1}{\operatorname{ln}⁡(2x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}{\int }_{1}^{2}\frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|){|}_{1}^{2} \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-\operatorname{ln}⁡1) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(\operatorname{ln}⁡2-0) \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x}\,⟹\,\text{d}u=\frac{1}{x}\,\text{d}x.
$$

Calculating the limits for $u$  gives the following:

| $x$ | ${e}^{2}$ | ${e}^{4}$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $2$ | $4$ |

We now substitute and evaluate, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\frac{8\operatorname{ln}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =8{\int }_{{e}^{2}}^{{e}^{4}}\operatorname{ln}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =8{\int }_{2}^{4}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =8\cdot {\frac{{u}^{2}}{2}|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =4\cdot {u}^{2}{|}_{2}^{4} \\  & =4\cdot (16-4) \\  & =48\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡4}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.

Calculating the limits for $u$ gives the following:

| $x$ | $1$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $u$ | $0$ | $1$ |

We now substitute and evaluate as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\frac{4{log}_{4}⁡x}{x}\,\text{d}x & =4{\int }_{1}^{4}{log}_{4}⁡x\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =4{\int }_{0}^{1}u\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡4\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡4{\int }_{0}^{1}u\,\text{d}u \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot \frac{{u}^{2}}{2}{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4\cdot (1-0) \\  & =2\operatorname{ln}⁡4 \\  & =4\operatorname{ln}⁡2\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
Let $u={log}_{7}⁡(4x).$ Differentiating, we get

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}=\frac{1}{x\operatorname{ln}⁡7}\,⟹\,\operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u=\frac{\text{d}x}{x}.
$$

Using the above, we can write the integral in terms of $u$ and evaluate:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{x{log}_{7}⁡(4x)}\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{{log}_{7}⁡(4x)}\cdot \frac{\text{d}x}{x} \\  & =\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \operatorname{ln}⁡7\,\text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\int \frac{1}{u}\cdot \text{d}u \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\operatorname{ln}⁡|u|+C \\  & =\operatorname{ln}⁡7\operatorname{ln}⁡|{log}_{7}⁡(4x)|+C\end{aligned}
$$
